title: Statistics - Lesson 10: Conclusions from Position Measures Practice
description: Practice using quartiles, IQR, percentile rank, and displays to support statistical conclusions.

questions.question: The ordered scores are 42, 48, 52, 55, 60, 64, 68, 70, 74, 78, 82. What is the median?
questions.explanation: There are 11 values, so the median is the 6th value in the ordered list, which is 64.

questions.question: For the data 42, 48, 52, 55, 60, 64, 68, 70, 74, 78, 82, the lower quartile is 52 and the upper quartile is 78. What is the IQR?
A smaller IQR means the middle half of the data is less spread out.
questions.explanation: IQR measures the spread of the middle half. A smaller IQR means those middle values are closer together.

questions.question: If Q1 = 30 and Q3 = 46, what is the IQR? Enter just the number.
A learner scored 74. In a group of 11 learners, 9 scores were at or below 74. About what percentile rank is this?
questions.explanation: 9/11 x 100 is about 81.8, so the learner is at about the 82nd percentile.

questions.question: Class A has median 64 and IQR 26. Class B has median 68 and IQR 14. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Class B has a slightly higher typical score and a more consistent middle half.
Class A must have every score lower than Class B.
Class B has no low scores.
Class A and Class B have the same spread.
questions.explanation: Class B's median is higher, and its smaller IQR shows a less spread-out middle half. The other statements overclaim.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why the statement 'The maximum is higher, so the whole group did better' is weak statistical reasoning.
questions.correctAnswer: A maximum describes only one value. A stronger conclusion should compare measures such as the median and IQR to describe more of the group.
questions.explanation: The answer should identify that the maximum is an extreme value and does not represent the entire distribution.

questions.question: Write an evidence-based conclusion from this information: Group B has median 34 minutes and IQR 8 minutes; Group A has median 32 minutes and IQR 15 minutes.
questions.correctAnswer: Group B has a slightly higher typical review time and more consistent middle-half review times because its median is 34 minutes and its IQR is 8 minutes, compared with Group A's median of 32 and IQR of 15.
questions.explanation: A strong response cites the median and IQR, then explains the meaning in the context of review time.
